title: What is known about 1RB1RD_1LC0LC_1RD1LB_1RF0RE_0RA1RE_---1RB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_1LC0LC_1RD1LB_1RF0RE_0RA1RE_---1RB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. A block of 110111 words grows at the left end; behind it a region of fixed length (16,724 cells since the event at sweep 8,347, step about 1.2·108) is transformed by a fixed map, checked against direct simulation over 9,000 sweeps. The region holds a reservoir of 2,758 words that a chaotic counter eats from the left. A shortened copy runs 4·106 more sweeps (about 3·1013 steps) without a halt.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 58,204 cells have been visited and 41,692 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The sweep map ignores the block
claims.text: At each visit of the left end in state B the tape is B>0 111 (011111)^n R (read rightwards); with n cut to 10 at every visit, R agrees with the true run at all of the first 9,000 visits except the event at visit 8,347.

claims.title: No halt in 4·10<sup>6</sup> more sweeps
claims.text: From visit 8,400 the shortened run makes 4·10<sup>6</sup> sweeps (about 3·10<sup>13</sup> steps of the true run) without a halt; no event changes R's length beyond the two-cell wobble of the block's phase.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.605). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The run is a fixed map applied to a region of fixed length, interrupted by rare events whose spacing grows exponentially; whether some event halts is not known.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0RB_1LC1RA_1LF0LD_0LE1LD_1LA1LC_---1LA up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. A block of six-cell words grows at every sweep; behind it a small region changes like a scrambled odometer, eating a long reservoir. This page runs the real machine in your browser and explains the pieces.

facts.text: The region after the block, since sweep 8,347.
4·10<sup>6</sup> sweeps of the shortened machine: no halt.
The reservoir left by the last event, to be eaten before the next.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: A growing block, a busy counter, and a reservoir
html: Run the simulator for a while and look at the tape each time the head reaches the left end. It always has the same four parts: a long uniform block (110111)n that grows by a fixed amount every sweep; next to it a short stretch that changes from sweep to sweep and looks random; then a long, regular reservoir; and at the far end an old region that never changes.

<svg viewBox="0 0 580 70" role="img" aria-label="The tape: a growing uniform block, an active counter region, a reservoir it eats, and a frozen old region" style="width:100%;max-width:620px;height:auto"><g font-family="var(--body)" font-size="11" fill="var(--fg2)"><text x="10" y="14">← grows 2 cells a sweep</text><text x="14" y="60">growing block</text><text x="184" y="60">active counter</text><text x="274" y="60">reservoir</text><text x="484" y="60">frozen</text></g><rect x="10" y="20" width="170" height="22" fill="var(--ink)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><rect x="180" y="20" width="90" height="22" fill="var(--heur-bg)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><rect x="270" y="20" width="210" height="22" fill="var(--accent-soft)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><rect x="480" y="20" width="90" height="22" fill="var(--sunk)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/></svg>

The head sweeps across the whole tape every time, which is why the visited part grows like the square root of the step count. Crossing the uniform block does nothing but cost time: the tape the head brings back does not depend on how long the block is. So from sweep to sweep the machine applies one fixed map to the part of the tape after the block, whose length stays exactly the same for long stretches of time.

Here the block is a run of words 011111 as read from the head (state B at the left end, after the cells 0 111), the reservoir is a run of 111101 words, and the old region at the far end is short. One event so far, at sweep 8,347: the region jumps from about 90 to 16,724 cells. Over 9,000 sweeps a version that cuts the block to 10 words at every sweep sees the same region as the real machine, the event included.

sections.heading: A counter that eats its reservoir, then refills it
html: The busy stretch behaves like an odometer with irregular digits: the cells right next to the block change at almost every sweep, cells further in change more and more rarely, and the deepest cell that has ever changed moves into the reservoir at a roughly constant number of cells per doubling of the number of sweeps, so crossing a reservoir takes a number of sweeps exponential in its length.

The busy stretch next to the block is about a hundred cells long and changes every sweep, as in 1RB1RC_1LC0RE_1LD0LB_1RA1LC_1RA0RF_---0RC; the 2,758-word reservoir behind it was intact in the samples taken up to 3·108 steps.

When the counter reaches the far end of the reservoir, something new happens (an event): the whole uniform block, by then very long, is turned into a fresh reservoir, and a new block starts growing from nothing. The next reservoir is as long as the block was, so the next event is exponentially further away than this one, and the one after that further still.

At the counter speeds of the related machines (tens of cells per doubling), a reservoir of 16,500 cells takes an astronomically large number of sweeps to cross; the next event is far beyond reach of simulation.

sections.heading: Halting needs the counter at the far end
html: The machine stops only in state F reading a 0, reached only as D>0 0 moving right (D writes a 1 and moves into F). Inside the block and the reservoir there are no two adjacent 0s, so a halt has to come from the busy stretch or the far end.

So a halt, if it ever comes, should come at an event, when the counter reaches the old region at the far end. Between events the machine just keeps sweeping (each event is exponentially further from the last), and at each event the outcome depends on the details of the old region, which look pseudo-random. A heuristic: if each event had a fixed chance of ending in a halt, the machine would halt with probability 1, but only after a tower of exponentials of steps; equally, a structural reason could make every event safe. Nothing here decides which.

sections.heading: What was checked, and how
html:
• The sweep map does not depend on the block length: resetsim ... check agrees with the real machine at every one of 9,000 sweeps (one event, at sweep 8,347).
  • From sweep 8,400 the shortened machine runs 4·106 sweeps (about 3·1013 steps of the real machine, estimated from the quadratic growth of the sweep time) without a halt.
  • Direct C simulation: no halt in 109 steps (triage); Lean: no halt in 107.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

family: counter eating a reservoir (bounded chaotic region, sweep map independent of the block)
summary: The same counter-eating-a-reservoir mechanism with a block of 110111 words: an event at sweep 8,347 (about 1.2*10^8 steps) made a 16,724-cell region with a reservoir of 2,758 words; no halt in 4*10^6 further sweeps.
